name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source, customizable CRM with REST and GraphQL APIs, workflows, AI agents, an app SDK and an MCP server, available as cloud or self-hosted.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code + PKCE and client credentials against the API

access.note: Free trial without credit card, self-hosting option; API included on all plans
Free self-hosted plan and cloud plans

api_surface.note: Core and Metadata APIs in REST and GraphQL, batch ops, rate limits
twenty CLI for data, metadata and raw API requests

mcp.note: Official MCP server at /mcp, with OAuth or API key

verdict.note: Documented API with self-serve API keys

notes: API keys are created in Settings > Developers; OAuth clients register dynamically (RFC 7591) with no vendor review. Rate limits: 50/min on Pro, 100/min on Organization. The MCP server also supports OAuth and API key. Whether creating API keys needs a workspace admin is not shown in the fetched pages.

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform offering APIs for SMS, WhatsApp, voice, email (SendGrid), user verification and conversational AI, usable by humans and AI agents.

auth.note: Lists OAuth 2.0, API Keys and Auth Token as supported methods; OAuth recommended for third-party apps
HTTP Basic auth with API key SID and secret

access.note: Free trial, no credit card required

api_surface.note: REST API at api.twilio.com covering accounts, numbers, calls, messages, usage

mcp.note: Official hosted Twilio MCP server at mcp.twilio.com/docs, public beta, read-only docs search

verdict.note: Documented REST API with self-serve credentials
Free trial signup and official SDKs

notes: Official MCP is public beta and read-only (docs search/retrieve, no API execution, no credentials); OAuth-authenticated execute tools are only planned. A self-hosted Twilio MCP server (Functions template/CLI plugin) is also mentioned. Webhooks exist; SDKs available.

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a B2B customer support and help desk platform that unifies Slack, Teams, email and chat threads and lets built-in or connected AI agents work inside them, exposed through a GraphQL API.

auth.note: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE for apps calling the API as a workspace user
Machine user API keys sent as a Bearer header

access.note: 7-day free trial, no credit card; Developer platform (API, Webhooks, MCP) is listed on the pricing page
Every plan starts with a free 7-day trial; no credit card needed

api_surface.note: GraphQL API with machine users and fine-grained API key permissions
MCP sits on top of the GraphQL API

mcp.note: Official remote MCP server at mcp.plain.com/mcp with ~400 tools, OAuth

verdict.note: API key creation is self-serve in workspace settings
Free trial without a credit card

notes: OAuth apps are created in Settings and work only in the workspace that created them. The MCP server is OAuth-only and is not counted as API auth. External Agents (Connected Agents) are listed under the Frontier plan. Admin requirements for installs are not shown.

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: HighLevel (GoHighLevel) is an all-in-one CRM, marketing automation and agency platform with a v2 REST API, OAuth 2.0 marketplace apps and an official MCP server.

auth.note: Authorization Code Grant for v2 APIs; client ID and secret generated in the app Auth settings
Mentions Private Integration Token as an alternative credential

access.note: Developer account signup; private apps for internal use, public apps need approval
Paid plans with a 14-day free trial; API access is listed as a core feature

api_surface.note: The MCP operation catalog spans 40 domains, which suggests a broad API

mcp.note: Hosted MCP URLs and OAuth setup

verdict.note: Documented OAuth flow, with a private app type available for internal use
Paid plans with a trial; Starter at $970/yr

notes: Private Integration Tokens (API key style) are mentioned only in the MCP help article, not in the auth docs fetched. Public Marketplace apps need approval. The location/agency admin must visit the install URL. Basic API access is listed under a plan tier, and the pricing page was partly truncated. The stoplight page was empty.

name: Sherlock
one_liner: Sherlock is an open-source Python CLI that hunts down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks, with results exported as txt, CSV or XLSX.

auth.note: Local MIT-licensed CLI; the README documents no credentials or API keys.

access.note: Free install via pipx, pip, uv or Docker; MIT license.

api_surface.note: CLI usage and flags (--json, --csv, --site, --proxy) documented in the README. There is no hosted API.

mcp.note: Third-party FastMCP server wrapping the Sherlock CLI. No official MCP was found in the sherlock-project README.

verdict.note: A wrappable local CLI counts as buildable_now.

notes: Only the GitHub README was fetched for the right product; the sherlockproject.xyz homepage was not. Pages for Sherlock Labs (observability), Sherlock Interview and Covertlabs are different products and were ignored. The CLI probes third-party sites, so their terms may restrict automated use.

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon's REST-based Selling Partner API (SP-API) lets sellers and vendors programmatically access orders, listings, inventory, fulfillment, reports, finances and more on Amazon's marketplace.

auth.note: OAuth authorization workflow, LWA token exchange

access.note: Roles must be requested and qualified for; architecture review; Appstore listing required for public apps
A paid Amazon seller account is also needed

api_surface.note: Large catalog of APIs: Orders, Listings, Feeds, Reports, FBA, Vendor, and more
REST-based API with sandbox and SDK generation

mcp.note: Describes a Selling Partner plugin (beta, US) for AI assistants; no MCP server URL or docs page given. The Ads MCP Server is a separate Amazon Ads product.
SP-API llms.txt checked; no MCP server listed in the fetched portion

verdict.note: Role qualification, architecture review and app listing make this approval-gated

notes: Private developers who only access their own seller account may have a lighter path, but fetched pages show registration, role approval and, for public apps, an architecture review and Appstore listing. The Selling Partner plugin for AI assistants is in beta with no MCP URL, so mcp_status is none. Seller admin requirement not shown.

name: Datadog
one_liner: Datadog is a cloud observability and security platform covering infrastructure, APM, logs and more, with a broad REST API, official client libraries and an official MCP server.

auth.note: API key plus application key required
OAuth2 authorization code flow with PKCE against the Datadog API

api_surface.note: HTTP REST API with official client libraries

mcp.note: Official Datadog MCP Server setup docs

verdict.note: Documented REST API with self-serve keys
New scoped auth model: PATs, SATs, OAuth clients

notes: Also supports scoped application keys, PATs, SATs and workload identity federation (per blog). The MCP server uses OAuth by default, with an API key fallback. Marketplace OAuth clients and OAuth client creation may need extra setup. The fetched pages do not show an admin requirement for API use.

name: Linear
one_liner: Linear is a project and issue tracking tool for software teams, with a GraphQL API, webhooks, a TypeScript SDK, an agent platform and an official hosted MCP server.

auth.note: OAuth2 authorization code, PKCE, client credentials; actor=app for agents
Mentions Linear API key / bearer token as a direct auth option

access.note: API and webhook access included on the Free plan, with no sales gate
Anyone can create an OAuth2 application

api_surface.note: GraphQL API, webhooks, attachments, customers, TypeScript SDK, agents docs

mcp.note: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
Changelog announcing the official MCP server

verdict.note: API and MCP access included on all plans, including Free

notes: Personal API keys are mentioned only on the MCP page (not in the fetched API docs); the OAuth page's mention that admin users access the OAuth app is not an install gate. MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. Third-party app management is a paid-plan admin feature, and workspace admins may restrict app installs.

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin is Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that writes, runs and tests code, with a v3 REST API, a CLI, and an official MCP server for managing sessions, playbooks and knowledge.

auth.note: Service user API keys and PATs, Bearer cog_ tokens

access.note: Free, Pro and Teams plans can be signed up for online. The Devin API row appears in the plan comparison.
Service user keys are provisioned in Settings > Devin API

mcp.note: Official Devin MCP server at mcp.devin.ai

notes: Creating service users needs org/enterprise admin settings access, but this is the customer's own account, not a vendor gate. Which plans include API access is not confirmed in the fetched pricing text. Legacy v1/v2 keys (apk_) are deprecated. The MCP server accepts the same cog_ keys; the CLI's MCP OAuth applies to third-party servers, not Devin's API.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent (gopaygent.com) is a payment gateway offering payments, subscriptions, payouts, fraud tools and a Connect product for marketplaces and platforms, with REST APIs, SDKs and Collect.js tokenization.

auth.note: cURL example uses a Bearer live key

access.note: Free plan and no credit card required

api_surface.note: REST APIs, SDKs, webhooks and sandbox
Docs cover the Pathfinder API, Collect.js and Three-Step Redirect

mcp.note: No MCP server or docs found on the fetched pages

verdict.note: Self-serve signup with a documented REST API

notes: Matched to gopaygent.com. The GitLab pages (Japanese Paygent module) and withpaygent.com (AI agent monetization) are different products and were not used. The docs page fetched is thin, so auth detail comes from the homepage cURL example. The Pathfinder API and Three-Step Redirect names suggest an NMI-style gateway, but the pages do not confirm it.
